unit: lowest floor above base flood elevation; no extra city freeboard
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale's floodplain chapter adds no freeboard number of its own for ordinary buildings, so the Florida Building Code's BFE + 1 ft applies. What the city does add is a two-year look-back: improvements are added up over two years when testing the 50% substantial-improvement line.

Zones are set parcel by parcel, so no single zone covers the whole city - check your own address. | NFIP history :: FEMA record: first flood hazard boundary map 3 Nov 1972; first FIRM 3 Nov 1972; regular NFIP program since 3 Nov 1972; entered CRS 1 Oct 1992. | Flood insurance discount :: CRS class 7 - 15% off NFIP premiums for policies in the Special Flood Hazard Area (class in effect 1 Oct 2020). | State minimum :: 2023 Florida Building Code, Residential R322.2.1 and R322.3.2 - lowest floor (A zones) or bottom of the lowest horizontal structural member (V and Coastal A zones) at BFE + 1 ft or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher. | Look up your zone :: City GIS Application (gis.fortlauderdale.gov/FemaFloodZones) or FEMA's Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov), the official public source for FIRMs.

unit: above BFE; homes also at least 9.0 ft NGVD
qualifier: Miami Beach sets a minimum freeboard of 1 foot and lets owners build up to 5 feet above base flood elevation without the extra height counting against zoning. In A zones a home's lowest floor and equipment must also clear 9.0 ft NGVD (7.44 ft NAVD) and the crown of road or sidewalk plus 1 foot, whichever is highest. Improvements are added up over one year.
detail_rows: Freeboard :: Minimum freeboard equals one foot; maximum freeboard equals five feet - Sec. 54-35. | Homes in A zones :: Lowest floor and service equipment no lower than 9.0 ft NGVD (7.44 ft NAVD), the crown of road or sidewalk plus one foot, or BFE plus minimum freeboard, whichever is higher - Sec. 54-48(1)(a). | Zone X :: Lowest floor at least 1 ft above the highest adjacent grade or the crown of the nearest street, whichever is higher - Sec. 54-48. | Substantial improvement :: Work during a one-year period with cumulative cost of 50% or more; includes substantial structural alteration and Alteration Level 3 - Sec. 54-35. | Seawall note :: For seawalls, a substantial improvement is repair costing $500 or more per linear foot - Sec. 54-61. | Worked example :: A building with a market value of $415,000 (structure only) crosses the 50% line once qualifying work within one year reaches $207,500; from then on the whole building must meet current flood-elevation rules. | Changing the rules :: Any ordinance that would reduce, relax, diminish or repeal Chapter 54 standards needs a five-sevenths vote of the city commission, and Article II amendments go first to the Florida Division of Emergency Management for review - Sec. 54-30. | FEMA flood map :: FEMA's Community Status Book (report dated 3 Oct 2026) lists Miami Beach as NFIP community 120651 with a current effective FIRM dated 11 Sep 2009. Zones are set parcel by parcel, so no single zone covers the whole city - check your own address. | NFIP history :: FEMA record: first FIRM 29 Sep 1972; regular NFIP program since 29 Sep 1972; entered CRS 1 Oct 1996. | Flood insurance discount :: CRS class 5 - 25% off NFIP premiums for policies in the Special Flood Hazard Area (class in effect 1 May 2019). | State minimum :: 2023 Florida Building Code, Residential R322.2.1 and R322.3.2 - lowest floor (A zones) or bottom of the lowest horizontal structural member (V and Coastal A zones) at BFE + 1 ft or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher. | Look up your zone :: Enter the address in FEMA's Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov), the official public source for FIRMs; an elevation certificate shows how your floor compares with the BFE.

headline_answer: 18-24 in above road, never below FIRM
unit: residential first floor vs adjacent road centerline
qualifier: Deerfield Beach ties first-floor height to the road as well as the flood map: a home's first floor goes 18 to 24 inches above the centerline of the adjacent roadway, and never below the FEMA map elevation. Its floodplain chapter uses the plain 50% substantial-improvement test.

Zones are set parcel by parcel, so no single zone covers the whole city - check your own address. | NFIP history :: FEMA record: first flood hazard boundary map 10 Nov 1972; first FIRM 10 Nov 1972; regular NFIP program since 10 Nov 1972; entered CRS 1 Oct 1992. | Flood insurance discount :: CRS class 8 - 10% off NFIP premiums for policies in the Special Flood Hazard Area (class in effect 1 Oct 2020). | State minimum :: 2023 Florida Building Code, Residential R322.2.1 and R322.3.2 - lowest floor (A zones) or bottom of the lowest horizontal structural member (V and Coastal A zones) at BFE + 1 ft or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher. | Look up your zone :: Enter the address in FEMA's Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov), the official public source for FIRMs; an elevation certificate shows how your floor compares with the BFE.

headline_answer: Higher of FBC or Broward future map
unit: lowest floor in special flood hazard areas
qualifier: Dania Beach builds to the future, not just today's map: new and substantially improved buildings go to the higher of the Florida Building Code elevation or the Broward County Future Conditions 100-year flood elevation. Its substantial-improvement test is 49%, counted over one year.

qualifier: Hallandale Beach labels its rule 'additional elevation (freeboard)': homes go to the Florida Building Code elevation or 18 inches above the crown of the adjacent roads, whichever is higher.
